chunks.title: [Cantonese Dubbed] CLO Official Tutorial Video ~ Basics Part p01 1. Making a T-shirt
chunks.content: # CLO Official Tutorial: Basics Part p01 – Making a T-shirt (Cantonese Dubbed) This document provides a detailed step-by-step guide on using CLO software for creating a T-shirt, focusing on file handling, panel editing, sewing techniques, simulation setup, and 3D costume quality enhancement. It covers important terminology such as panel duplication, Edit panel tool, Cron link panel, linear sewing tool, arrangement points, and simulation processes. --- ## Importing and Preparing Pattern Files This section explains how to import pattern files into CLO, view them in 2D and 3D windows, and prepare the panels for editing by duplicating halves and aligning them with virtual model shadows. - Locate the **Fifi** file in *Ametar* and *Vimeo VR*. Open it by double-clicking or dragging into the 3D window. - In the practice file **B-Basic-A-Tissue**, find and open the **Tissue.dxf** file similarly. - Click **OK** in the import menu. - In the 2D window, observe the gray shadow representing the virtual model. - Select all panels (shortcut: Ctrl + A) and move them onto the virtual model shadow. - Note only half of each panel is visible; duplicate the other half for symmetry. - Use the **Edit panel tool** from the 2D toolbar: - Right-click on the front middle line and select the Edit panel tool. - Repeat on the back middle line. - Sleeves are separate panels and require a different approach. --- ## Editing Panels and Synchronizing Symmetrical Parts This section covers advanced panel editing techniques using the **Edit panel tool** and **Cron link panel** to ensure symmetric modifications and sewing lines on paired panels like sleeves. - For sleeves, right-click on the panel in the 2D window and select **Cron link panel**. - Right-click and choose **Edit panel**. - When modifying or creating a sewing line on one side, the other side automatically mirrors the changes. - Hold **Shift** to align panels precisely. - Use the **Rearrange 2D** tool from the 3D toolbar to synchronize all panel arrangements with the 3D window. - To display model arrangement points, enable **Show Arrangement Point** in the 3D ruler. - Some arrangement points may be obscured by panels; reposition panels on these points for proper alignment. --- ## Aligning Panels to Arrangement Points This section explains how to position panels onto the model’s arrangement points to ensure proper fit and alignment in the 3D model. - Select all panels (Ctrl + A) in the 2D window. - Drag panels onto corresponding arrangement points visible in the 3D window. - For the front panel, click and drag to the front arrangement point. - Press the shortcut key to switch to rear view. - Select the rear panel and position it on the rear arrangement point. - Use mouse controls and **Ctrl** key to fine-tune panel placement on angles.

chunks.title: [Cantonese Dubbed] CLO Official Tutorial Video ~ Basics Part p01 1. Making a T-shirt
chunks.content: --- ## Aligning Panels to Arrangement Points This section explains how to position panels onto the model’s arrangement points to ensure proper fit and alignment in the 3D model. - Select all panels (Ctrl + A) in the 2D window. - Drag panels onto corresponding arrangement points visible in the 3D window. - For the front panel, click and drag to the front arrangement point. - Press the shortcut key to switch to rear view. - Select the rear panel and position it on the rear arrangement point. - Use mouse controls and **Ctrl** key to fine-tune panel placement on angles. --- ## Sewing Lines with the Linear Sewing Tool This section details using the **linear sewing tool** to sew garment parts such as shoulders, side seams, sleeves, and collars, emphasizing the importance of sewing line direction and completing symmetrical sewing sets. - Select the **linear sewing tool** from the 2D toolbar. - Sew the shoulder line, side seams, and sleeves; each sewing operation requires two lines to complete the set. - Pay attention to the direction of the sewing lines for proper garment assembly. - Sew the collar to the big body: - Start with the front collar and front piece. - Use shortcut key 8 to rotate the view to rear. - For gaps (e.g., between baskets), use the linear sewing tool with a stroke set to **N**. - Click on the back collar near the center and complete the sewing set. - Hold **Shift** and select **N** to continue sewing along the back center and side seams. - Complete the linear sewing process before proceeding. --- ## Simulation Setup and Fabric Application This section describes how to load simulation files, position the virtual model, apply fabric textures, and run the simulation smoothly in CLO. - After sewing, turn off simulation. - Open the **post file** located in the *Aventa FemaleVR* folder. - Double-click the **FV203** file or drag it into the 3D window. - Confirm dialogue prompts by clicking **OK**. - Adjust the virtual model to a vertical position. - Import the **NEAT** fabric file from the picture window into the object window. - Apply the fabric onto the FemaleVR model. - Activate the simulation, then close it to finalize fabric application. - Open **FV203** in the **FB app** via the FB menu bar. - Confirm prompts with **OK** to run the simulation smoothly. - The FB application interface will show a light blue color when the simulation starts. - Click **OK** to begin simulation. --- ## Enhancing 3D Costume Quality This section explains how to improve the visual quality of the 3D garment within CLO by adjusting settings and using the attribute editor. - In the 3D toolbar, select the tool to **increase costume quality**. - Open the dialogue box and confirm with **OK**. - Open the model and apply the new quality settings to the 3D costume. - In the object window, select the plant object related to the garment.

chunks.content: --- ## Enhancing 3D Costume Quality This section explains how to improve the visual quality of the 3D garment within CLO by adjusting settings and using the attribute editor. - In the 3D toolbar, select the tool to **increase costume quality**. - Open the dialogue box and confirm with **OK**. - Open the model and apply the new quality settings to the 3D costume. - In the object window, select the plant object related to the garment. - Use the **attribute editor** to adjust appearance attributes. - Click the color bar to open the color dialogue box. - Use the small eyedropper tool to extract colors from the page, or manually enter RGB values. --- # Summary This tutorial covers the foundational workflow in CLO for creating a T-shirt, including file importing, panel editing and duplication, panel alignment via arrangement points, sewing techniques using the linear sewing tool, simulation setup with fabric application, and improving 3D garment quality. Key tools and commands include the Edit panel tool, Cron link panel, Rearrange 2D, linear sewing tool, FB app for simulation, and attribute editor for color and appearance adjustments.
